title: Psalm 42: As the Deer Pants for Water
summary: Far from the temple, a worshiper thirsts for God like a deer panting for streams. Mocked by people who ask “Where is your God?” and haunted by memories of leading festival crowds to God's house, he speaks to his own downcast soul and tells it to hope in God. The psalm moves between despair and hope, with the same refrain in verses 5 and 11.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 42

line: Far from the temple, a worshiper thirsts for God like a deer for water, hears people ask where his God is, and talks back to his own downcast soul: hope in God.
guide: Do what verse 5 does: ask your low soul why it is so low, then tell it where to look. That is not pretending to be fine; it is choosing where to look while you are still low. Hope is said again and again, so read on into Psalm 43, which finishes the poem.

care.text: No one should read this psalm and decide what is wrong with someone else. It does not say why he is low, and it gives no single cure. If ‘my tears have been my food both day and night’ is true of you now, please do not carry it alone. Tell someone you trust: a doctor, a pastor or a friend. If you have thoughts of hurting yourself, speak to someone today. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: Tears, taunts, and memories of festival worship
Refrain: why are you downcast, O my soul
Despair far from Zion, and God's love by day and night
Why have You forgotten me? The enemies' taunt

verses.t: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah. As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God.
My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When shall I come and appear in God’s presence?
My tears have been my food both day and night, while men ask me all day long, “Where is your God?”
These things come to mind as I pour out my soul: how I walked with the multitude, leading the procession to the house of God with shouts of joy and praise.
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence.
O my God, my soul despairs within me. Therefore I remember You from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon— even from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me.
The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me as a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God my Rock, “Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?”
Like the crushing of my bones, my enemies taunt me, while they say to me all day long, “Where is your God?”
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
